_note: The rules glossary behind every gilded word in the UI (U1, ui/common/glossary.gd). Text is our own words. `from` borrows the text kept elsewhere so it lives in one place: condition:<id> (data/conditions), action:<id>, property:<id> and mastery:<id> (combat/action_catalog.gd). `match` lists the exact phrases that open the term (default: its name; [] means only See also reaches it); `after` limits a match to text that ends with one of these just before it, and `unless_next` rules out a match followed by one of these. `here` says how this game plays the rule where it differs. `see` names related terms.

terms.name: D20 Test
terms.text: The three rolls that decide whether an attempt works: ability checks, saving throws and attack rolls. Roll a d20, add your modifiers, and meet or beat the target number: a Difficulty Class for checks and saves, Armor Class for attacks.

terms.name: Ability Check
terms.text: A d20 plus one ability's modifier against a Difficulty Class, rolled when the outcome of something you try is in doubt. Your Proficiency Bonus is added when a skill or tool you're proficient with applies.

terms.name: Saving Throw
terms.text: A d20 roll to resist something done to you: a spell, a trap, a poison. Add the named ability's modifier, plus your Proficiency Bonus if your class makes you proficient in that save, and meet the effect's Difficulty Class. Every class is proficient in two.

terms.name: Attack Roll
terms.text: A d20 plus the attack's ability modifier, plus your Proficiency Bonus for a weapon you're proficient with or a spell. It hits if the total equals or beats the target's Armor Class. A 20 on the die always hits, as a Critical Hit; a 1 always misses.

terms.name: Difficulty Class
terms.text: The number an ability check or saving throw has to reach. 5 is very easy, 10 easy, 15 medium, 20 hard, 25 very hard and 30 nearly impossible. A spell's DC is its caster's spell save DC.

terms.name: Armor Class
terms.text: How hard a creature is to hit: an attack roll has to equal or beat it. Unarmored it's 10 + your Dexterity modifier; armor, a Shield and some features change the sum.
terms.here: Hover Armor Class on the character sheet to see each part of yours.

terms.name: Advantage
terms.text: Roll two d20s and keep the higher. Several sources still give only the two dice, and if anything also gives Disadvantage on the same roll, the two cancel out and you roll one d20.

terms.name: Disadvantage
terms.text: Roll two d20s and keep the lower. Several sources still give only the two dice, and any Advantage on the same roll cancels it, however many sources each side has.

terms.name: Proficiency Bonus
terms.text: A bonus that grows with character level: +2 at levels 1 to 4, +3 from 5, +4 from 9, +5 from 13 and +6 from 17. It's added to attacks with weapons you're proficient with and with spells, to the saves and skills you're proficient in, and to your spell save DC.

terms.name: Expertise
terms.text: For a skill you have Expertise in, add twice your Proficiency Bonus to its checks instead of once.

terms.name: Passive Perception
terms.text: 10 + your Wisdom (Perception) bonus: how alert you are without searching. A hidden creature or trap whose DC it meets is noticed without a roll.

terms.name: Critical Hit
terms.text: A 20 on the d20 of an attack roll hits whatever the target's Armor Class, and the attack's damage dice are rolled twice and added together (its modifiers count once). A creature at 0 Hit Points that takes one fails two Death Saving Throws.

terms.name: Heroic Inspiration
terms.text: While you have it, you can spend it to reroll any one die right after you roll it, and you must use the new roll. You can hold only one at a time. A Human gains it after each Long Rest, and some feats and features give it out.
terms.here: On a failed saving throw the game spends it for you, unless that character's setting for it is Never: saves can't pause for your choice yet.

terms.name: Hit Points
terms.text: How much harm a creature can take. Damage lowers them and healing restores them, never above the Hit Point maximum. A character who drops to 0 falls Unconscious and starts making Death Saving Throws; most monsters simply die.

terms.name: Bloodied
terms.text: A creature is Bloodied while it has half its Hit Points or fewer left. Some features and monsters change what they do once someone is Bloodied.
terms.here: A Bloodied creature's Hit Point bar turns a brighter red.

terms.name: Temporary Hit Points
terms.text: A cushion that takes damage before your Hit Points do. They don't add up: if you'd gain more while you still have some, you keep one amount or the other. Healing can't restore them, and they're gone after a Long Rest unless they run out or a feature ends them sooner.
terms.here: The game keeps the larger amount for you.

terms.name: Hit Point Dice
terms.text: One per character level, their size set by your class (a d8 for a Cleric, a d10 for a Fighter). During a Short Rest you can roll as many as you like, adding your Constitution modifier to each, and regain that many Hit Points. A Long Rest gives back every one you've spent.

terms.name: Death Saving Throw
terms.text: At the start of each turn you spend at 0 Hit Points, roll a d20 with nothing added: 10 or higher is a success, anything lower a failure. Three successes and you're Stable; three failures and you die. A 1 counts as two failures, and a 20 brings you back with 1 Hit Point. Taking damage at 0 Hit Points is a failure, two if it's a Critical Hit.

terms.name: Stable
terms.text: A creature at 0 Hit Points that has stopped dying. It makes no more Death Saving Throws but stays Unconscious until it regains Hit Points, and any damage sets it dying again.
terms.here: After a fight is won, any party member still dying is made Stable: their friends tend them.

terms.name: Initiative
terms.text: When a fight starts, everyone rolls Initiative (a Dexterity check), and the totals set the order of turns from highest to lowest. The order holds for every round of the fight.

terms.name: Surprise
terms.text: A combatant caught off guard as a fight breaks out has Disadvantage on its Initiative roll.
terms.here: When the party sneaks up, its lowest Stealth total is checked against each enemy's Passive Perception.

terms.name: Bonus Action
terms.text: A swift extra deed that some spells and features let you do on your turn besides your action. You get one Bonus Action a turn, and only when something gives you a use for it.

terms.name: Reaction
terms.text: An instant response to a trigger, such as an Opportunity Attack or the Shield spell, and it can happen on someone else's turn. You have one per round; it comes back at the start of your turn.

terms.name: Opportunity Attack
terms.text: When a creature you can see leaves your reach, you can use your Reaction to make one melee attack against it. A creature that took the Disengage action doesn't provoke one, and neither does one moved without spending its own movement (pushed, pulled or teleported).

terms.name: Speed
terms.text: How many feet a creature can move on its turn; each square is 5 feet. You can split the move around your actions. Difficult Terrain, standing up from Prone and several conditions eat into it.

terms.name: Difficult Terrain
terms.text: Ground that's hard to cross: rubble, thick undergrowth, deep snow, a crowd. Every foot of movement through it costs an extra foot, so a 5-foot square takes 10 feet of Speed.

terms.name: Cover
terms.text: Something between you and whatever attacks you. Half Cover (a low wall, another creature) gives +2 to Armor Class and Dexterity saving throws; Three-Quarters Cover (an arrow slit, a thick tree trunk) gives +5; Total Cover means you can't be targeted directly at all.

terms.name: Unarmed Strike
terms.text: A punch, kick or headbutt made in place of a weapon attack. It can deal damage (an attack roll with Strength and your Proficiency Bonus, for 1 + your Strength modifier in Bludgeoning damage), or instead Grapple or Shove the target, which then makes a saving throw rather than you rolling to hit.

terms.name: Attack
terms.text: Make one attack with a weapon or an Unarmed Strike, or more with Extra Attack. You can draw or stow one weapon as part of each attack.

terms.name: Magic
terms.text: Cast a spell whose casting time is an action, or use a magic item or a magical feature that calls for the Magic action.

terms.name: Influence
terms.text: Try to change a creature's mind with words or presence: a Charisma check (Deception, Intimidation, Performance or Persuasion), or Wisdom (Animal Handling) for a beast, against a DC set by how it feels about you.
terms.here: Nothing you fight in Barovia will be talked down mid-battle.

terms.name: Utilize
terms.text: Use an object that takes an action to use, such as pulling a lever or working a Healer's Kit.

terms.name: Shove
terms.text: One of your attacks, made with an Unarmed Strike: a target no more than one size larger than you makes a Strength or Dexterity saving throw against 8 + your Strength modifier + your Proficiency Bonus, or is pushed 5 feet away or knocked Prone (you pick which).

terms.name: Concentration
terms.text: Some spells last only while you keep your mind on them. You can concentrate on one spell at a time, so starting another ends the first. It also ends if you're Incapacitated or die, and whenever you take damage you make a Constitution saving throw (DC 10 or half the damage, whichever is higher, up to 30) or lose it.

terms.name: Spell Slot
terms.text: What a spellcaster spends to cast a spell of level 1 or higher. A spell takes a slot of its own level or higher, and a higher slot often makes it stronger. Spent slots come back after a Long Rest.

terms.name: Cantrip
terms.text: A level 0 spell, cast as often as you like with no spell slot. Most cantrips grow stronger at character levels 5, 11 and 17.

terms.name: Ritual
terms.text: A spell with the Ritual tag can be cast without a spell slot if you take 10 minutes longer over it. You need the spell prepared; a Wizard can read it from the spellbook instead.

terms.name: Spell Save DC
terms.text: 8 + your spellcasting ability modifier + your Proficiency Bonus. A creature resisting one of your spells has to meet it with its saving throw.

terms.name: Spell Attack
terms.text: An attack roll made with a spell: a d20 + your spellcasting ability modifier + your Proficiency Bonus against the target's Armor Class.

terms.name: Pact Magic
terms.text: A Warlock's spellcasting: only a few spell slots, but all of them at the Warlock's highest slot level, and every spent one returns after a Short or Long Rest.

terms.name: Attunement
terms.text: Some magic items work only for a creature bonded to them. A creature can be attuned to at most three items at once, and a cursed item won't let go until its curse is lifted.
terms.here: Attuning, and ending it, happen at once from the inventory instead of taking a Short Rest.

terms.name: Emanation
terms.text: An area that spreads out in every direction from a creature or object and moves with it. The creature at its centre isn't affected unless the effect says so.

terms.name: Sphere
terms.text: An area spreading in every direction from a point, its size given as a radius. Total Cover blocks it.

terms.name: Cube
terms.text: A cube whose one face touches the point it comes from; its size is the length of each side.

terms.name: Cone
terms.text: An area that widens as it goes out from its point of origin: at any distance its width equals that distance, and its length is the cone's size.

terms.name: Cylinder
terms.text: A circle with a height, given as a radius and a height. It usually rises from the ground or falls from above.

terms.name: Short Rest
terms.text: An hour of downtime: eating, binding wounds, reading. You can roll Hit Point Dice to heal, and features that recharge on a Short Rest come back.

terms.name: Long Rest
terms.text: Eight hours, most of them asleep. You regain all your Hit Points and every spent Hit Point Die, your spell slots and most features, and your Exhaustion drops by one level. Only one Long Rest a day.

terms.name: Dim Light
terms.text: Twilight, moonlight, the outer reach of a torch's glow. Everything in it is Lightly Obscured.

terms.name: Bright Light
terms.text: Daylight, or close to a torch or a lantern. Creatures in it can be seen normally.

terms.name: Darkness
terms.text: Night with no moon, an unlit cellar, or magical darkness. Everything in it is Heavily Obscured.

terms.name: Lightly Obscured
terms.text: Dim Light, patchy fog or light foliage. Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on sight have Disadvantage there.

terms.name: Heavily Obscured
terms.text: Darkness, thick fog or dense foliage blocks sight entirely: anyone trying to see something there is effectively Blinded.

terms.name: Darkvision
terms.text: Within its range you see in Dim Light as if it were Bright Light, and in Darkness as if it were Dim Light, though only in shades of grey.

terms.name: Blindsight
terms.text: Within its range a creature perceives everything without needing eyes, so darkness and invisibility hide nothing from it there. Total Cover still does.

terms.name: Truesight
terms.text: Within its range a creature sees through normal and magical darkness, sees Invisible creatures and objects, sees through visual illusions, and sees a shapechanger's true form.

terms.name: Tremorsense
terms.text: Within its range a creature can tell where others are and what moves, as long as they touch the same ground or liquid it does.

terms.name: Resistance
terms.text: Damage of that type is halved, rounded down. Several sources of Resistance to the same type count as one.

terms.name: Vulnerability
terms.text: Damage of that type is doubled. Several sources count as one.

terms.name: Immunity
terms.text: Damage of that type, or the named condition, doesn't affect the creature at all.

terms.name: Weapon Mastery
terms.text: Every weapon has a mastery property: Cleave, Graze, Nick, Push, Sap, Slow, Topple or Vex. A character whose class grants Weapon Mastery can use the property of a few chosen kinds of weapon, and can change those picks after a Long Rest.
